purpose: Derive the shared VICTOR source transformation from the governing fabrication specification. Existing source is migration input, not design authority. Return only the prescribed JSON replacement edits. Do not invoke tools; this is one bounded source derivation, not an autonomous project. Do not generate or request private tests. No direct edits or deployment. Preserve every clause, refuse if required interface evidence is missing. Before strings must each match exactly once in application order. Match original SHA256 from inputs for every edit. No new files/dependencies. Keep replacements minimal while fully implementing the contract.

workOrder.text:
---
title: Fabrication of an authored VICTOR home from a public content cell
date-created: 2026-09-27
type: specification
status: closed behavioral work order; generation admission pending independent assay custody
derived-from: 2026-09-27-muse-assist-public-site-lld.md
derived-from-sha256: accb11b20cbbbac42f4b45d05db7cbfb20f0344becaa2a389e69d3bd13ed44a1
realization-contract: 2026-09-27-muse-assist-fabrication-lld.md
realization-contract-sha256: b55a7b9cd27054b2e5ddf6a06463409d22a400176f15196ff921d20dac85fff2
---

## What this is

This fabrication work order derives the generic authored-home transformation required by L-S04/L-S05 of the [public-site LLD](2026-09-27-muse-assist-public-site-lld.md). It governs a source-free behavioral derivation and constrained codemod of VICTOR, preserving its default publication behavior while allowing a published content cell to be the canonical narrative at `/`. It contains no implementation body or prescribed private test source; current code is transformation input and migration evidence.

## Authority and constraints

**F-H01.** The work MUST follow L-S04–L-S07, H-F1–H-F4, and R-14–R-16 through the predecessor chain. The local [code-fabrication specification][fabrication-rule] supplies source derivation, assay ordering/custody and rejection rules. These project engineering rules are the applicable authority; no external standards certification follows from using VICTOR's existing conformance checks. Existing source and dependency rights MUST remain unchanged.

**F-H02.** The change MUST use VICTOR's existing catalog, content reader, renderer, projection collision handling, artifact inventory and release verifier. It MUST NOT introduce a second renderer/parser, application-specific template, publication database, scheduler, model gateway, package dependency or browser framework. The output is transformed shared publisher source and associated documentation/assay evidence, not deployed site assets.

## Input and output contracts

**F-H03 — Home option.** `build` and the normalized project configuration MUST accept the same union:

| Input | Defined behavior |
|---|---|
| Omitted or `true` | Preserve existing root index/archive behavior |
| `false` | Preserve existing root omission/custom-projector behavior |
| Nonempty string naming one catalog cell | Render that published cell as the authored root |
| Null, array, object, other primitive, empty/whitespace name | Record a configuration refusal; result is not releasable |

The selected name is a catalog identity, not a file path or arbitrary URL. Selection MUST resolve to exactly that cell; aliases MUST NOT silently select another cell. A duplicate catalog identity remains a catalog refusal. A missing cell or one excluded by the build's `drafts` policy MUST refuse. Explicit preview `drafts:true` MAY render a potential cell, but the resulting preview MUST NOT establish release under `drafts:false`. Neither invalid selection nor refusal may fall back to a plausible-looking accepted index.

**F-H04 — Projection output.** The existing build result shape `{artifacts, artifactRecords, report, catalog, site}` MUST be preserved. With valid authored home selection it MUST contain exactly one root narrative, the selected cell's ordinary route as a noindex redirect to `/`, other published pages with their existing routes, and existing optional projections under the selected configuration. The cell's identity, content address, publication membership, references and evidence MUST NOT be mutated merely to make its URL empty. No raw source or runtime object MUST enter a public artifact.

## URL correspondence

**F-H05.** One resolved canonical page URL MUST govern HTML canonical links, social metadata, structured-data page identity, reference resolution, feeds and sitemap. For the selected home this is the site's origin with trailing `/`; other cells retain their original URLs. A site's WebSite identity and its home page identity MAY share a URL but MUST retain their correct structured-data types/relationships without a self-containing page assertion. Redirect targets MUST be ordinary root-origin URLs, never protocol-relative `//` values produced by concatenating an empty name.

Existing renamed-from aliases of the selected home MUST resolve to `/` without loops. References, backlinks, chapter entries, archive entries and TUFTE navigation to that cell MUST lead to its canonical root. The sitemap MUST include the root once and MUST NOT list the selected cell's redirect as a canonical page. Feeds retain the same content/identity and use the canonical page URL. The implementation MUST preserve direct callers' default rendering/resolver behavior when no home-route option is supplied.

**F-H06.** With authored home and archives enabled, the authored cell owns `/`; the archive projector MUST omit only its competing root artifact and retain its non-root date/section/tag/type/status routes. It MUST NOT silently move existing archive paths to invented destinations. Navigation whose stated purpose requires the omitted complete publication listing MUST either use an existing truthful archive route or be omitted; it MUST NOT label the new product page as that listing. With Boolean home options, existing archive behavior remains unchanged. A competing custom/public-asset root MUST retain the normal collision refusal instead of overriding either artifact.

## Transformation boundary

**F-H07.** The generator MUST receive the predecessor chain digests, this order, the current bytes of declared transformation inputs, their dependencies/interfaces needed to preserve behavior, and public examples. Existing source is reference/codemod input; it MUST NOT replace the behavior clauses. No private assay material may enter its context, tool results, filesystem or inherited conversation. The source result MUST identify each changed path, resulting bytes/digest, input digest, and clause correspondence; it MUST NOT apply its own patch to the shared checkout.

The first captured inputs were refused as stale before generation. Concurrent work added the string homepage selector and a bindinggenerations.net consumer. The revised order preserves that selector and consumer effect while completing canonical correspondence. No source was generated under the stale revision. Current transformation inputs, re-read for this revision:

| File | SHA-256 |
| [src/build.mjs](../../../../../../../../../../../../computer-knowledge-systems-services-section/apps/static-site-publisher/src/build.mjs) | `de4a1252849b6164fb474007f74ffe59401259d5185564317c00520e9c07d730` |
| [src/config.mjs](../../../../../../../../../../../../computer-knowledge-systems-services-section/apps/static-site-publisher/src/config.mjs) | `1f0ebaef65e7a551b672e1f7790c6c7f4153323f3ccfe5c24c3b672d3ad5c80f` |
| [src/catalog.mjs](../../../../../../../../../../../../computer-knowledge-systems-services-section/apps/static-site-publisher/src/catalog.mjs) | `399ee4bae62828d28f52a750898398d2e0b22f3239e96708ea1b76054eca6d62` |
| [src/page.mjs](../../../../../../../../../../../../computer-knowledge-systems-services-section/apps/static-site-publisher/src/page.mjs) | `f25e8728d26fa61c2fdf9549a58e0fc41aca2eff712a7435a051f5980dd568d9` |
| [src/feeds.mjs](../../../../../../../../../../../../computer-knowledge-systems-services-section/apps/static-site-publisher/src/feeds.mjs) | `66806b5a6b5b462c12beabd966344d58694d7db01a25c5eb5cd8f92945c1998d` |
| [src/tiles.mjs](../../../../../../../../../../../../computer-knowledge-systems-services-section/apps/static-site-publisher/src/tiles.mjs) | `7c18b229db8e5a38c982fc71f2a43c781dfb93fd8b93c8ccb9ec15b242dda61a` |
| [src/publication-archives.mjs](../../../../../../../../../../../../computer-knowledge-systems-services-section/apps/static-site-publisher/src/publication-archives.mjs) | `f37cd3509e4dfee0a3d90542350303eda9f9a75bc991a985bdb5a83461b249a5` |
| [README.md](../../../../../../../../../../../../computer-knowledge-systems-services-section/apps/static-site-publisher/README.md) | `8bf413b63bebe8cf7ae9bce4f034fc86fcd4e48d15c52d6876be0d55c1b0a641` |

Other existing shared URL/projection consumers may require changes if inspection establishes they participate in F-H05. Before adding an affected file, the derivation MUST bind its current bytes/digest and record why the existing correspondence requires it; unrelated cleanup is prohibited. Existing imports/dependency versions MUST be preserved unless the closed behavioral contract proves a change necessary and a revised work order admits it. New dependencies are prohibited by F-H02.

**F-H08.** Candidate materialization MUST occur outside the shared checkout. Promotion MUST compare every changed input against the captured digest immediately before replacement. A changed input causes `stale-input` refusal; no force overwrite or automatic merge of uninspected concurrent changes is allowed. Obsolete special-case root generation, if any is found within this change, MUST be removed once the shared route demonstrates the same effect. This order does not authorize deletion of unrelated code, data, or existing site outputs.

## Public examples and independent acceptance

The following examples constrain behavior without prescribing private assays:

- A published cell named `overview`, selected by `home: "overview"`, supplies the root body. `/overview/` redirects to `/`; a different cell linking to `overview` links to `/`.
- Omitted `home` still generates the usual publication root. `home:false` still permits a custom root projector without a built-in competing root.
- A selected cell absent from the catalog causes a refusal. A selected potential cell is refused in release mode and available only in an explicitly enabled draft preview.
- Selecting a home while another projector claims `index.html` causes a collision refusal. A theme-only change does not rename the selected cell or alter its address.

**F-H09.** Behavioral assays MUST be derived before source and held outside the generator's accessible context under F-H07. They MUST cover the input union; default/false compatibility; Markdown body at root; canonical/social/structured-data consistency; alias/reference/feed/sitemap/archive/TUFTE links; missing/draft/duplicate selection; collision refusal; unchanged-input repeatability; and stale-input promotion refusal. The assessor MUST exercise the actual build and inspect rendered navigation and metadata in the generated artifacts. Structural admission or a schema pass alone is insufficient.

**F-H10.** Acceptance evidence MUST bind work-order/input/candidate/assay digests and record method, environment, assessor identity, outcomes and limitations. The existing generic receipt's locator+digest MAY refer to this richer evidence bundle; it MUST NOT claim to contain or validate that evidence itself. Failed candidates remain rejected. A revised candidate MUST have changed governing evidence or specification with a recorded derivation, not an invisible post-test hand patch.

## Implementations

VICTOR already supplies Markdown detail rendering, Boolean root selection and a partially realized string selector, route collision detection, artifact provenance and release checks. Its hard-coded cell URLs and current Boolean root checks are migration obligations, not reasons to add a Muse-only renderer. No candidate has yet been derived or accepted under this work order.

## Open questions

- **F-HO1 — Provider custody:** The [bounded realization LLD](2026-09-27-muse-assist-fabrication-lld.md) selects an operator-mediated isolated Luna invocation and independent assessment using existing tools. Its L-F04 boundary probe and actual model availability remain admission conditions. An unrestricted shared-checkout subagent is not substituted for that boundary.
- **F-HO2 — Assay custody:** The assessor must commit the independent assay bundle before the source provider receives the admitted order. Exact private assay content is intentionally absent here; acceptance method and coverage are governed by F-H09.

realizationContract:
---
title: Bounded source derivation and independent assessment for muse-assist
date-created: 2026-09-27
type: specification
status: derived LLD; operator-mediated realization using existing tools
derived-from: 2026-09-27-muse-assist-hld.md
derived-from-sha256: 5f824fb118e4cdfec8e23cc2f74e8aff667eff420d5e461ffb4c60b8ad57c6e9
---

## What this is

This LLD closes H-F2/H-F3's first source-derivation realization using existing inference and isolation tools, without adding a scheduler, gateway, generator framework, or application-specific fabricator. It governs an operator-mediated transformation from a closed fabrication order into a staged candidate and separately held acceptance evidence. It is a bounded first realization, not automation of the whole Customer Demand-to-code chain.

## Work-order and candidate carriers

**L-F01.** The admitted generation input MUST bind the predecessor chain, fabrication order, current transformation-input bytes/digests, public examples, output contract, model/configuration and invocation bounds. The input MUST exclude private assay source, fixtures, expected results and assessor conversation. A separate assessor MUST derive and commit the private assay inventory before source derivation starts. Commitment is a byte digest, not proof that the assay is sufficient.

**L-F02.** The first output contract is a closed JSON object with `disposition` (`candidate` or `refused`), `reason`, and `edits`. A refused result MUST have no edits and a specific reason. Each candidate edit MUST contain exactly `path`, `inputSha256`, `before`, `after`, and `clauses`. `path` identifies an admitted relative source file, `inputSha256` binds its original bytes, `before` is a nonempty exact substring occurring once at the point of application, `after` is replacement text, and `clauses` is a nonempty array of governing clause IDs. Multiple edits to a file apply in output order against one original input digest. Missing files, ambiguous text matches, path escape, mismatched input digest, unrecognized clause IDs, or extra object fields MUST refuse materialization. Candidate outputs are untrusted source until independently assessed.

The deterministic materializer applies only admitted textual replacements to a staged copy and computes full resulting file digests. This is a bounded codemod application, not behavioral source derivation. It MUST NOT execute generator-provided shell commands. New files require a separately specified creation contract; this first work order uses existing files. Actual transformed bytes, input/output digests and clause correspondence become the source-result evidence required by H-F2/F-H07.

## Generator access boundary

**L-F03.** The source provider MUST run in a fresh inference context with no inherited conversation, no assessor material, and no shared-checkout write access. For the first local realization, the existing Codex executable MAY be invoked noninteractively with the requested GPT-6 Luna model inside a Bubblewrap mount/PID namespace. The only task content is the public input packet delivered on standard input. The host checkout, assay directory, host process namespace, session history, user/project configuration, skills and connectors MUST NOT be mounted or otherwise supplied. The public output schema MAY be mounted read-only. Runtime libraries, TLS/DNS files and the existing authentication file may be made available solely to run the authenticated provider; authentication material MUST NOT be printed or placed in prompts.

The invocation MUST use a fresh ephemeral session, ignore user configuration and rules, disable shell, web search, apps and further agent delegation where the installed CLI supports those controls, and use a read-only model-command sandbox. External process isolation supplies the filesystem boundary; prompts and the CLI's read-only setting alone do not. Native tools which remain advertised cannot see the omitted mounts. The invocation MUST NOT resume this conversation or any previous source/assessor session. The actual argument vector, executable digest/version, public input digest, observed model and event record MUST be retained without credentials. Undeclared tool use, unexpected mounts, source input change, unavailable authentication/model, or source-provider access to assessor material MUST reject that invocation. No alternate model is silently substituted.

**L-F04.** Before live source generation, a deterministic process under the same mount profile MUST establish that the host checkout and an external sentinel cannot be read, that the process view is namespaced, and that only the intended task inputs are available. This demonstrates the local process boundary, not provider-server confidentiality or model correctness. The provider's own server retention/isolation remains a trust assumption and MUST be stated. The operator MUST NOT send private assay content through feedback, diagnostics or a resumed source session.

## Independent assessment and promotion

**L-F05.** The assessor MUST run the committed assays against the content-bound candidate, separately from the source provider. Executing candidate code MUST not give it a communication channel back to that provider or access to operational credentials/private user data. A network-denied execution namespace with only required runtime, dependency, candidate and assay inputs is the selected local assessment boundary. The assessor may inspect private results; the source generator receives only a separately admitted public reproduction or changed specification, never private fixtures or raw assay logs.

**L-F06.** The evidence bundle MUST contain specification/chain/input/candidate/assay digests, provider/model/configuration, invocation boundaries, method, environment, assessor, result, limits, and measured token/time/cost information where available. Missing cash-cost data MUST be marked unavailable rather than zero. Generic artifact receipts may reference this bundle by locator/digest; receipts do not prove acceptance. Failed candidates remain rejected. New evidence or revised specifications can justify a new candidate; an invisible edit after a failed assay cannot.

**L-F07.** Promotion MUST compare each original input digest with current shared-checkout bytes immediately before applying the accepted replacements. Any mismatch refuses the entire promotion batch and preserves both candidate and concurrent edits. All affected files must pass this check before any is replaced. Promotion MUST retain the accepted output digest and actual receiving-workflow evidence; staging checks do not establish public deployment or assistant operation.

## Implementations

The installed host currently has Bubblewrap and Codex CLI 0.154.0. A preliminary empty namespace probe could not see `/home/emsenn/info`; the complete invocation profile still requires L-F04's recorded check. The CLI's local help exposes ephemeral, ignored-user-config, output-schema and noninteractive execution. [Official configuration documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference) defines the shell-tool switch; [noninteractive documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) describes the ephemeral invocation. These are invocation capabilities, not proof of assay independence or generated-code correctness.

The separately inspected ops inference route reported one configured `llama3.2:3b` provider with no admitted resource-availability observation. It was not invoked or substituted for the requested Luna source role. Its existence is not evidence of available capacity. The local invocation above uses existing tooling; no inference service is being repaired or reimplemented here.

## Open questions

- **L-FO1:** The first source invocation must establish actual model/authentication availability and record L-F04's complete boundary check. Failure preserves the closed order and assays; it does not authorize direct hand coding.
- **L-FO2:** Broader unattended generation, scheduler integration and automatic demand-to-design derivation are not supplied by this operator-mediated protocol. Any subsequent automation must preserve these contracts and receive its own specification before implementation.

README.md.text:
# static-site-publisher (VICTOR)

VICTOR — Voxelized Information Catalog Topos Orienting Relations — is Red Cup Engineering's website framework. Its competitive mandate is to meet and beat current website frameworks. It assembles one content-addressed catalog of related content, then composes downstream domain applications, HTTP serving, pages and assets, feeds, structured data, federation, conformance, and release custody into coherent websites. TUFTE, the Tiling User Form Topology Engine, is VICTOR's user-interface framework; it is not an optional decorative renderer.

The lower applications remain useful independently. VICTOR owns catalog assembly, composition, release policy, and cross-projection checks; it does not need to reimplement every protocol or replace a site's domain runtime.

The name is grounded in the corpus's own apparatus:

- **Voxelized** — content cells addressed by RFC 6920 `ni:///sha-256` identifiers, stored and released in content-address-sharded form.
- **Information Catalog** — the RWIL log → state → record → content tiering, with the Belnap knowledge order read as an information order.
- **Topos** — the `R = Sh(T,J)` sheaf framing and the seven closure conditions; sheaf gluing as the deterministic-merge test for partial catalog views.
- **Orienting Relations** — RMN, the Relation Model Notation, as the typed term language for the relations the catalog serves.

VICTOR carries forward the useful behavior of the `semantic-site-server` lineage (dual-mode serving, RDF/JSON-LD projection, feeds, Cool URIs, pluggable readers, and build reports) by realizing those concerns as composable live applications. It consumes TUFTE as the topology, user-form, interaction, and rendering engine for browser interfaces.

Conformance targets are the real, current standards — the WHATWG HTML Living Standard, WCAG 2.2, ARIA in HTML — checked continuously at build time, not claimed once at launch. The study of these targets lives in the Living Web Science Services Section.

## Contents

- `content/text/documents/articles/notes/` — the governing documents: the SAS, the mandate note, and the self-sufficient companion specifications (TUFTE contract, dialect, design rules, standards facts, engineering practices).
- `src/`, `scripts/`, `test/` — the fusion application, runnable entrypoints, and executable contract tests.

## State: 0.1.7, a walking skeleton that walks

`victor build <contentDir> <outDir>` renders a complete site; `victor check` runs the double-build determinism check; `victor serve` watches and serves with drafts visible, and `victor serve --release` serves the release without drafts or a watcher; `victor new` scaffolds a typed cell. The tested walking skeleton includes content-addressed cells, relational Markdown with GFM pipe tables and citations against a CSL-JSON front-matter references block, papers whose chapters are ordered and content-addressed cells in their own right, accessible page rendering, OpenGraph and Twitter-card meta on every rendered page, theme validation, complete and paged publication archives, section/tag/type/status indexes, RSS 2.0, Atom 1.0 and JSON Feed 1.1, browser search, sitemap, robots policy, a 404 page, TUFTE atlas and neighborhood projections, project configuration, deterministic build reports, and recursive byte-preserving public assets with collision protection.

## Website framework boundary

Downstream applications import VICTOR, not its HTTP server or TUFTE dependencies. `createVictorWebsite()` owns the whole build, application-composition, TUFTE projection, serving, and rebuild lifecycle:

```js
import { createVictorWebsite } from '@red-cup-engineering/victor';

const researchApplication = {
  resources: [{
    id: 'research-status',
    match: '/api/research',
    methods: ['GET'],
    handler: () => ({ status: 200, body: 'research ready' }),
  }],
};

const website = await createVictorWebsite({
  contentDir: new URL('./content', import.meta.url).pathname,
  site: { name: 'Research application', baseIri: 'https://research.example/' },
  applications: researchApplication,
});

website.watch();
await website.start({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: 8561 });
```

`applications` uses the shared HTTP application contract and receives VICTOR's rebuild-aware catalog context when supplied as a factory. `website.rebuild()` replaces generated website state without recreating stateful downstream applications. `website.close()` closes watchers and drains the shared upstream server. The `victor serve` command uses this same public boundary rather than carrying a private second implementation.

## Composition

A `victor.config.mjs` may export `publicDir`, `site`, `theme`, and an `applications` factory. The factory receives the current build, a dynamic `listPublications()` view, and `fetchApplication()` for adapting route-scoped Fetch handlers. It returns one or more applications using the shared HTTP application contract. VICTOR composes those first, then its redirect application and the lower `serve-http-artifact-inventory-service` release application. A live rebuild updates the artifact inventory, redirects, and `listPublications()` without recreating stateful lower applications. The runtime uses the shared observability preset for correlation IDs, W3C trace context, Server-Timing, and private request metrics by default; a profile may publish the metrics resource or explicitly disable the preset. Shared `/healthz`, `/livez`, and build-aware `/readyz` resources are enabled by default and may be renamed, extended, or disabled through the runtime `probes` option.

The project configuration is versioned and closed. It may also provide a `content-reader/v1` reader and additional build projectors. The default filesystem reader supplies content digests, provenance, and dependencies instead of letting VICTOR walk files itself. Built-in archive, page, TUFTE, theme, feed, discovery, redirect, and public-asset projections use the shared projector contract; additional projectors receive the normalized build context. Every artifact retains its projector/source provenance, and path collisions block release rather than relying on insertion order.

`home: false` omits VICTOR's default home projection so a domain projector can own the root route. Its artifact remains subject to the same collision checks as every other projection. `home: '<cell name>'` gives the root route to that published cell (a site's own home page), rendered as its page, in place of the catalog listing; the cell keeps its own route too, and a name that is not a published cell is a refusal.

Publication archives are enabled by default with 20 items per page. Set
`archives: { pageSize: 40 }` to change that bound, or `archives: false` when a
site supplies its own index projection. VICTOR renders the neutral lower
archive projection through its ordinary escaped HTML shell and shared theme.
Every collection has a complete `/archive/` route as well as paged
routes; collisions with cells, redirects, and other archive routes are release
diagnostics.

An optional `pwa` configuration enables the shared progressive-web-app
projector. It runs as a deliberate second phase after the ordinary artifact
inventory is complete, deriving a deterministic web app manifest, precache
inventory, content-addressed cache name, service worker, and offline behavior.

Public search is enabled by default. The shared search projector runs after
HTML rendering and emits a deterministic weighted index plus a zero-dependency
browser query module; VICTOR supplies an accessible `/search/` interface. It
understands Pagefind-compatible body, ignore, metadata, and filter annotations.
Set `search: false` to omit the page and assets, or pass a search configuration
object to select paths, limits, stop words, and output locations. Search runs
before the optional PWA phase so its assets can be precached.

Browser asset transformation is enabled by default between ordinary projection
and search. The lower inventory transformer gives CSS and JavaScript final-byte
fingerprinted names, rewrites local HTML/CSS/module references, adds SHA-384 SRI
to script and stylesheet loads, assigns immutable cache metadata, and emits
`asset-manifest.json`. Set `assets: false` to preserve source filenames, or use
`assets` to select paths, extensions, hash length, integrity, and manifest path.

Feed serialization also lives below VICTOR. The shared projector emits RSS,
Atom, and JSON Feed artifacts with explicit media types; VICTOR maps catalog
publications to that neutral item contract and advertises all three formats in
rendered page heads.

Protocol endpoints are advertised only when they are actually configured. A
`discovery` object accepts `webmention`, `micropub`, `indieauthMetadata`, and
one or more `me` URLs; VICTOR validates them and emits the corresponding HTML
`link` relations across its rendered surfaces. This keeps page discovery in
the renderer while the receiving, authorization, and custody behavior remains
in the lower Webmention, Micropub, IndieAuth/OAuth, and ActivityPub apps.

A `release-manifest.json` is enabled by default and projected last,
after search and the optional PWA phase. The shared release-candidate service
records every completed artifact's path, public URL, byte length, SHA-256 `ni`
identity, and available media/cache/provenance metadata. It excludes itself and
`report.json` to avoid recursive identities; the report carries the manifest
identity and summary. `victor check` now compares two independently built
manifest identities. After `victor build` writes the output directory, it also
uses the lower verifier to check the materialized files against that manifest;
missing, changed, linked, or unexpected files fail the command. Set
`release: false` to omit it, or configure its profile, metadata, path, and
explicit exclusions through `release`.

Every rendered HTML artifact passes through a rendered-HTML conformance stage
as soon as projection completes (SAS §9.3, checks C-01, C-02, C-03, C-09,
C-10, C-12, and C-15 as embedded machine subsets: doctype, title, and unique
ids; the ARIA-last rule against explicit roles that restate native semantics;
the document language; heading hierarchy over the whole page, not only the
authored body; an alt attribute on every image; JSON-LD that parses and types
every node; and the orientation anatomy of a title, exactly one `h1`, a
`main`, and a `nav` on every indexable page). A finding is an ordinary refusal
naming the check and its catalog code (`R-13`, `R-14`, `R-10`, `R-11`, `R-12`,
`R-09`), so a failing page blocks release like a broken link does; a missing
`lang`, a link without an accessible name, and an image without intrinsic
dimensions are `A-03` advisories, the last because VICTOR does not yet
measure images. The stage runs over projector-supplied pages too, and VICTOR's
own pages pass it under test. Set `conformance: false` to omit it. What the
stage does not do is stated plainly: it is not a WHATWG validator, it does not
compute per-page contrast (the theme is certified at build time instead), and
C-04, C-05, C-07, C-11, and C-16 remain to be wired.

The completed candidate is also checked by the shared static-site conformance
service before it is called releasable. HTML references must resolve to an
artifact in the manifest or to an explicitly configured same-origin protocol
endpoint. Broken paths, unsafe URL schemes, and origin escapes become
ordinary build refusals. Remote preview probing remains a separate, injected-
fetch operation (also exposed by the lower `probe-static-site-release` command)
so provider credentials and traffic changes stay outside VICTOR.

The ActivityPub publication profile plugs into this seam: give `createPublicationActivityPubProvider()` the supplied `listPublications`, then wrap its `fetch` with `fetchApplication` and a predicate covering its actor, inbox/outbox, NodeInfo, and `.well-known` routes. Authentication, keys, inbox custody, and delivery remain ActivityPub application concerns; VICTOR supplies publications and composition.

Current product gaps are recorded without shrinking the mandate: transclusion, mathematics, and raw-HTML passthrough are not yet implemented; images are copied but not yet processed into modern formats (so intrinsic dimensions are advised, not enforced); there is one built-in template rather than the resolution cascade; nine of the sixteen SAS conformance checks are still not wired into the build; and richer structured-data projections (beyond the JSON-LD and OpenGraph/Twitter-card meta now emitted) and federation remain to be composed or implemented.
